title: Stopping and Starting
tagline: How to pause on a word, what the Mushaf's stop signs mean, and how to begin again.
intro: Nobody recites a long verse in one breath. This level teaches you how to stop correctly (waqf), what the little signs above the text tell you, and how to restart (ibtida) when a word begins with a connecting alif.

lessons.title: How to Stop
lessons.summary: Stopping changes the end of a word: the last vowel drops away and the word ends on a sukun.
explain: Rule 1: a final fathah, kasrah or dammah is replaced by a sukun. ٱلنَّاسِ becomes an-naas.
Rule 2: tanween. Fathatan becomes a long 'aa' (عَلِيمًا is 'aleemaa'). Kasratan and dammatan are simply dropped (أَحَدٌ is 'aḥad').
Rule 3: the round ta (ـة) becomes a soft haa: ٱلْقَارِعَةُ is al-qaari'ah.
Rule 4: a madd letter just before the final letter may be stretched 2, 4 or 6 counts (Level 3). A qalqalah letter at the end bounces (Level 4).
Every verse ending is a natural place to stop.
how: Finish the word as usual until the last letter.
Replace the last vowel with a sukun and let your breath relax.
lessons.spot: The end of a verse. Or any word marked with a stop sign.
tips: Stopping is a skill: train it on verse endings first.
mistakes: Pronouncing the final vowel or tanween when stopping.

examples.note: ٱلنَّاسِ: the kasrah becomes a sukun. Say 'an-naas'.
تَوَّابَۢا: fathatan becomes a long 'aa'. Say 'tawwaabaa'.
ٱلْقَارِعَةُ: the round ta becomes haa. Say 'al-qaari'ah'.

cards.q: What happens to fathatan (ـً) when you stop?
cards.a: It becomes a long 'aa': عَلِيمًا is 'aleemaa'.

cards.q: What happens to kasratan and dammatan when you stop?
cards.a: They are dropped: أَحَدٌ is 'aḥad', خُسْرٍ is 'khusr'.

cards.q: What happens to the round ta (ـة) when you stop?

lessons.title: The Mushaf's Stop Signs
lessons.summary: The small marks above words tell you whether to stop, to continue, or that either is fine.
explain: مـ (ۘ): you must stop. Continuing would change the meaning.
لا (ۙ): do not stop. If you must (for breath), restart a few words back.
ج (ۚ): stopping and continuing are equally fine.
قلى (ۗ): stopping is better than continuing.
صلى (ۖ): continuing is better than stopping, but you may stop.
∴ ∴ (ۛ): two dots in two places: stop at one of them but not both.
س (ۜ): a short silent pause (saktah) without taking a breath.
how: Notice the sign after each word.
tips: Verse ends are always safe to stop on, even without a sign.

showcase.note: ∴ ∴: stop at one of the two, not both.

lessons.title: How to Start
lessons.summary: When you start on a word that begins with a connecting alif (ٱ), you must add a short starting vowel.
explain: The article ٱلْ and the name ٱللَّه start with a fathah: ٱلْحَمْدُ is al-ḥamd.

Verbs: look at the vowel of the THIRD letter (counting the alif as the first). If it is a dammah, start with a dammah: ٱنظُرْ is un-ẓur. Otherwise start with a kasrah: ٱهْدِنَا is ih-di-naa, ٱقْرَأْ is iq-ra'.
Nouns such as ٱسْم and ٱبْن start with a kasrah: ism, ibn.
how: Spot the connecting alif at the start.
Choose the starting vowel by the rule above.
lessons.spot: A verse that begins with ٱ.
tips: Fathah for ال and Allah, kasrah for most, dammah only when the third letter has a dammah.
mistakes: Starting with the wrong vowel, for example a fathah on ٱهْدِنَا.

examples.note: ٱهْدِنَا: the third letter has a kasrah, so start with kasrah. Say 'ih-dinaa'.
ٱقْرَأْ: the third letter has a fathah, so start with kasrah. Say 'iq-ra''.
ٱنظُرْ: the third letter has a dammah, so start with dammah. Say 'un-ẓur'.

cards.q: How do you start on ٱلْ (the article)?
How do you choose the starting vowel of a verb that begins with ٱ?
cards.a: Look at the vowel of the third letter (the alif counts as the first). Dammah gives dammah (ٱنظُرْ = un-ẓur). Otherwise start with kasrah (ٱهْدِنَا = ih-dinaa).
